correctness.rationale: For x in the augmentation ideal of an abelian p-group algebra, x^exp(G)=0, so multiplication by x has kernel dimension at least |G|/exp(G); equality is attained by g-1 for an element g of maximal order. Accounting for whether x^2=0 gives the exact minimum-degree formula, and comparison under graph isomorphism yields exponent invariance.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The 2014 modular group-ring result recovers field, order, abelianness, cyclicity, and over the prime field rank, but no exponent invariant or minimum-degree formula was located. Targeted searches across synonymous formulations and later group-ring graph literature found no matching theorem; the main residual risk is an implicit observation in unindexed literature.

value.rationale: The theorem adds exponent to the group invariants visible in modular zero-divisor graphs and, together with the known rank invariant, settles the graph-isomorphism question for every two-generated finite abelian p-group over the prime field.
